title: Counting the Days the Young-Driver Surcharge Is Charged Over on a Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
Once a Keyturn Trip Booking has been running for at least 7 days, the days the young-driver surcharge is charged over are counted to the scheduled return rather than to the day the surcharge is raised, and where they start depends on whether the guest took the vehicle on the first day of the reserved period.

**Where the trip started later than the first day of the reserved period and has run for at least 7 days**, the days charged run from the day the trip actually started to the scheduled return, the day of return counted.

**Where the trip started on the first day of the reserved period and has run for at least 7 days**, the days charged run from the first day of the reserved period to the scheduled return, the day of return counted.

**In every other case** the days charged are the days the trip has already run, counted from the day the trip actually started to the day the surcharge is raised with that day counted.

The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The three conventions

| The day the trip actually started | Days the trip has run | Counted from | Counted to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Later than the first day of the reserved period | 7 or more | The day the trip actually started | The scheduled return, that day counted |
| The first day of the reserved period | 7 or more | The first day of the reserved period | The scheduled return, that day counted |
| Either | Fewer than 7 | The day the trip actually started | The day the surcharge is raised, that day counted |

Seven days is reached rather than passed: a trip that has run exactly 7 days takes one of the first two conventions.

*Hypothetical.* A reserved period running from the 1st to the 20th of a month, on which the guest actually took the vehicle on the 4th and the surcharge is raised on the 12th. The trip has run 8 days, which is at least 7, and it started later than the first day of the reserved period, so the days charged run from the 4th to the 20th with the 20th counted: 17 days.

*The same reserved period where the guest took the vehicle on the 1st.* The trip has run 11 days and started on the first day of the reserved period, so the days charged run from the 1st to the 20th with the 20th counted: 20 days.

*The same reserved period where the guest took the vehicle on the 9th and the surcharge is raised on the 12th.* The trip has run 3 days, fewer than 7, so the days charged run from the 9th to the 12th with the 12th counted: 4 days.
